original_text: Similar results have been reported by \cite{Dimauro22}, who studied a sample of massive galaxies at $0<z<2$ on the SFR-M$_\star$ plane, finding galaxies with minimal bulge components ($B/T<0.2$) are all on the SFMS while galaxies with significant bulges ($B/T>0.2$) are responsible for the bending of main sequence at high-mass end.
injected_text: Similar results have been reported by \cite{Dimauro22}, who studied a sample of galaxies on the SFR-M$_\star$ plane, finding galaxies with minimal bulge components ($B/T<0.2$) are all on the SFMS while galaxies with significant bulges ($B/T>0.2$) are responsible for the bending of main sequence at high-mass end.
rationale: Dimauro22 explicitly restrict their analysis to a sample of massive galaxies in the redshift range 0<z<2; dropping both the mass-selection ('massive') and redshift-range ('at $0<z<2$') qualifiers over-generalises their result to galaxies of all masses at all redshifts, while the cite key, the B/T thresholds, and the directional claim are preserved.
ground_truth_description: Removed the scope qualifiers 'massive' and 'at $0<z<2$' from the citing sentence describing Dimauro22's sample, broadening the cited result beyond the regime in which it was demonstrated.

rationale: Inserts a spurious 1/2 prefactor in front of the log on the RHS of the modified Lee+15 main-sequence parameterisation (Eq.1); this is the kind of dropped/misplaced normalisation factor a tired author could plausibly introduce, and it breaks the paper's own stated property that 'this function reduces to the Lee15 parameterization when gamma_2=0' (Lee15 has a full log, not (1/2) log), so Wolfram can refute it symbolically. ground_truth_description: A factor of 1/2 was inserted in front of the log term on the right-hand side of Eq. (1), corrupting the normalisation/prefactor of the modified Lee+15 main-sequence functional form.

truth.term_role: normalisation prefactor on the log term (should be unity to recover the Lee+15 limit when gamma_2=0; halving it shifts the function by an extra (1/2)log factor and breaks the stated reduction property)
